 Akhilesh Yadav Calls for Aadhaar-Linked Voting, Metal Cards to Prevent Poll Rigging
 By ANI | Updated: November 9, 2026 15:11 IST 
 Preferred on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has urged for Aadhaar cards to be linked with voting and biometric identification for ...
 Open in App Akhilesh Yadav Calls for Aadhaar-Linked Voting, Metal Cards to Prevent Poll Rigging
 Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has urged for Aadhaar cards to be linked with voting and biometric identification for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. His proposal aims to prevent electoral rigging and ensure fair polls.
 Yadav, in a recent statement, emphasized the need for a robust system. “Simple, straightforward demands regarding the election: Aadhaar cards should be linked to voting. Instead of paper or plastic, ‘metal cards’ should be made so they cannot be forged. Fingerprint or iris-based biometric identification should be adopted because no two people have the same biometrics, so the BJP will not be able to rig the vote,” he stated.
 This demand surfaces amidst ongoing protests by Opposition parties, including the INDIA bloc, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The Opposition has called for Kumar’s resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise, raising concerns about its implications for voter lists.
 Uttar Pradesh is gearing up for Assembly elections next year, where the Samajwadi Party is keen on making a strong comeback after facing defeats in the 2017 and 2022 elections. The party sees these proposed reforms as crucial for a transparent electoral process.
 Separately, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi also highlighted a series of election-related concerns, including the SIR, proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha seats, and the now-scrapped electoral bonds. He accused the ruling party of various practices, including breaking opposition parties and making hate speeches during campaigns, alongside questioning the reliability of EVMs. These concerns underscore a broader debate among political parties regarding electoral integrity.
